After Myra and the baby left, I had Shirley home for a month.
We spent a lot of time sewing• Shirley made two dresses, with my
help, and I made two.
One a navy blue sheer wool, which I am very
pleased with.
The other, a print, I am not too sure about. I haven't
worn it yet,
as it doesn't look just like the victure did. Before
Shirley went back, Angela was quite sick.
I spent as much time with
her as I could.
Her cousin and I took turns.
She finally had a nurse
during the day, and I stayed with her at nights.
The doctor wanted
her to go to the hospital, but she didn't want to. She had pneumonia.
She is quite all right now. Myra has had bronchitas for the last
two weeks, and I have been going over there in the daytime. Mrs.
Klaus has kept Joelle. I am going over this afternoon. Yesterday
I went over and took her to the doctor and she seemed to feel a
little better. She went back to work last Tuesday,
but had to stop
on Thursday.
The doctor is giving her oromizen, (I don't know how to
spell it,, and it seems to be helping her.
I went with Bee Hatie the other night to see Lowell Thomas'
pictures of Tibet.
They were so interesting, and in the end they
gave F.A.A. quite a bit of advertising.
Have you seen it? I am afraid
that is the way I am going to do my traveling.
I am so glad you are
having such a wonderful trip, and everything has turned out as you
had hoped it would.
That was interesting about Clarance Young. I thought he was
Off P. A. A• I heard that he resigned because he thought he wasn't
being treated right.
I was so sorry to hear about the Bonds. I had some friends
to luncheon the other day, among them was Mrs. Kroll, who always
speake to kindly about Harold and Mr. Bond.
Harold and re
She is very nice.
I had Pat Taggart, who asked to be rememberedto yo when I wrote,
Nellie Sharp and Mercedes Me Micking, and Angela, and two others
whom you don't know.
They all seemed to be so congenial, and it
was all very pleasant. I was so far behind as I have been rather
tied down the last few months.
I have a wonderful gadget I want to send. you when you get
settled at home. It is a dispenser for hand cream, and just gives
one the proper amount.
It is like a cole cream jar,
and is not
bad looking. I have one in my bedroom and one in the kitchen.
I must leave you. I don't know whether this will ever catch
up with you. I am so sorry I didn't get it written before you left
Paris.
Dearest love to you and Hebe, and very best wishes to
Harold. You have more than paid me back for anything we ever
did for you.
I can't tell you how much my visit with you meant
to me. I just forgot everything, and enjoyed every minute with
you, besides all the wonderful shows. I think of it all, most
every day. I do love you all very much.
As ever,
elma.

April 22nd, 1950.
Dearest Debby:
You have been wonderful about writing, and I do
believe I have received all your letters. I think our letters
papers, you will understand.
I have never heard anymore fron
Russaks about the blouse they claimed I hadn't paid for, nor
from Harold's secretary. I sent her my cancelled check, and I
suppose it has been taken care of.
I am not very systematic, and
I was glad that I had that cancelled eheck, as it would have
been
embarrassing.
I was so sure that I had paid for it, but I couldn't
remember just how I thought I had had it sent c. o. Do
I was so interested in your letter from Baguio.
ane wished so much I could have been there.
Elsa wants me to
come out so badly, but I am not sure that I could take it. I
wouldn't want to leave Shirley anyway, until she is more settled.
She has been sick again, and they wanted to give her an extended
leave of absense.
Frankly, I don't care whether she finishes or
not.
It has changed her so much, I don't know whether it is
what they must come up against, or whether it is the roommate she
is so fond of.
She is older than Shirley, and to me, and most
everyone that has met her, most unattractive. She has a very
disgruntled attitude about everything.
I thought if Shirley
can't finish, I would send her to Medical Secretarial School.
I think she would be good at that.
She was out to the City
and County Hospital for communicable deseases, and said it
was very interesting,
but when it came time to send her in the
I. B. ward, the doctor's out there sent her back to st. Lukes
and said they didn't think she was strong enough. She has had
a cough for such a long time. She smokes much too much, and
they told her at St. Lukes she would have to give up smoking,
and they would keep her on there for awhile, but if she doesn't
get rid of her cough, she would have to take an extended leave.
So much has happened in the last few months.
had Myra and the baby for a couple of months, until they could
find a place. I loved having the baby,
but it did keep me
very busy.
I know how the girls must feel when they get them
all tucked away safely in bed at night.
Myra has found a little
apartment, which is not palatial by any means, but it is much
better than the other place she had to live in.
She married Lou
on the 26th of March.
They went up to Nevada, and I kept the babi
for her. She seems to be very happy, and says that he is so good
to her. She wants to work for a few months, which I don't
approve of, and yesterday Lou told me that he had been begging
her to stop. I shall try and talk to her again, but she doesn't
pay tomach attention to my advice.
I told ou, I thought he
should be firm with her, and not let her have her own way. He
said he would try, but I think heris too easy going. She has a
very good place for the baby now.
A German woman,
who is a trained
nurse and has a lovely garden.
She has one other little girl the
same age as Joelle, and they do have fun together.
A PaINISAPOS
